speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me exactly how long these symptoms have been present and if the swelling is constant or fluctuates?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the mechanism of injury involving a jersey pull suggests a significant force was applied to your ring finger. Was the finger deformed or visibly crooked at the moment of injury, or did you hear a "pop" sound? Additionally, is there any numbness or tingling in the finger currently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to flex the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint and the extension of the finger at rest strongly suggest a disruption of the extensor mechanism or a specific tendon injury. Given the mechanism of injury where the finger was forced into extension or hyperextension while flexed, can you confirm if the finger was bent backward against your will during the collision? Also, does the pain radiate up the finger, and is the swelling localized specifically to the tip or the entire finger?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: The mechanism of injury involving a forceful pull on a flexed finger, combined with your inability to flex the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint and the finger resting in extension, strongly suggests an extensor tendon injury. Can you confirm that you felt a specific "snap" or "pop" at the time of injury, and are there any visible gaps or depressions over the top of your finger tip? Additionally, I need to see the area to check for lacerations or a retracted tendon; would you allow me to request images of your right hand? REQUEST IMAGES: Right_hand_extensor_injury.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The absence of fever and neuropathic symptoms makes infection unlikely, but the specific clinical signs you described—extensor lag at the DIP joint and the finger resting in extension—are classic for an extensor mechanism tear. Given the mechanism of injury and your symptoms, I believe you have sustained a mallet finger injury.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Tendon Avulsion/Disruption of the Extensor Mechanism at the Distal Interphalangeal Joint).

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
